pages.text: "I want to reach too!" Lulu jumped toward a high kitchen shelf lined with dried figs. The cousins could reach on tiptoe. Lulu was far too short.
More jumps, but the fingertips brushed only air. "Why am I so little?" Lulu's ears drooped. Lulu slipped beneath the big table and sat.
Dim and quiet below, Lulu buried a face in the knees. Something rolled over—a dropped wooden spoon.
"Where is the spoon?" came a voice above. Uncle Nino, straw hat tipped back, bent down. But he was too tall to fit.
Lulu handed him the spoon. "Wow! I cannot get in, but Lulu fits right in!" He patted his long legs and laughed.
Stirring a pot, Mom asked, "Anything else down there?" Lulu crawled and searched. One fork, one garlic clove! "Little Lulu fits right in!"
Dinner preparations began. Uncle Nino reached up for figs. The cousins carried plates. Lulu carried the ladle beneath the table, slipping between chairs.
Lulu's bell jingled below. "The bell tells us where Lulu is!" The cousins laughed. Under the table, Lulu laughed too.
Now they split the table-setting jobs three ways. "One, tall Uncle gets the high shelf! Two, cousins above the table! Three, little Lulu below!" Dinner was ready in a blink.
Mom hugged Lulu and rubbed cheeks together. "You being little makes things easier at home." Little ones have special jobs too. "Little Lulu fits right in!" Under the table went Lulu again!
